subject: General Knowledge
description: Nicknames of cities, leaders, sports figures: very high hit in Indian exams

questions.stem: The city known as 'the CITY OF NAWABS' in India is:
questions.explanation: Lucknow — capital of Uttar Pradesh, associated with the courtly culture of Awadh under the Nawabs (Asaf-ud-Daula onwards). Hyderabad is 'City of Pearls' / 'City of Nizams'. Jaipur is 'Pink City'. Bhopal is 'City of Lakes' / 'City of Begums'.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: 'PUNJAB KESARI' (Lion of Punjab) is a nickname of:
questions.explanation: Lala Lajpat Rai was one of the 'Lal-Bal-Pal' trio of extremist leaders. Died after police lathi-charge during the anti-Simon-Commission protest in Lahore, 1928. 'Lion of Punjab' is his title. (Maharaja Ranjit Singh is called 'Sher-e-Punjab'.)
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Match the NICKNAME with the PERSONALITY. A. Father of the Nation.  B. Iron Man of India.  C. Frontier Gandhi.  D. Deshbandhu. List-II: 1. Mahatma Gandhi.  2. Sardar Patel.  3. Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan.  4. C. R. Das.
questions.explanation: Gandhi — 'Father of the Nation' (Subhas Chandra Bose gave this title in 1944). Patel — 'Iron Man / Sardar' for integrating princely states. Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan — 'Frontier Gandhi' / 'Bacha Khan' for Pashtun non-violent activism. Chittaranjan Das — 'Deshbandhu' (Friend of the nation).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which Indian state is known as 'THE LAND OF FIVE RIVERS'?
questions.explanation: Punjab = 'panj' (five) + 'ab' (waters/river) in Persian. The five rivers: Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, Sutlej. Three now flow through Pakistan (under the Indus Water Treaty 1960, Pakistan gets the western rivers — Indus, Jhelum, Chenab — with some use; India gets Ravi, Beas, Sutlej).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The CITY OF GOLDEN TEMPLE is:
questions.explanation: Amritsar houses the Harmandir Sahib (Golden Temple) — holiest Sikh gurudwara, founded by Guru Ram Das (4th Sikh Guru) and built by Guru Arjan Dev (5th Sikh Guru). Varanasi is 'City of Temples' / 'Spiritual Capital'.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: 'GRAND OLD MAN OF INDIA' was the nickname of:
questions.explanation: Dadabhai Naoroji — 'Grand Old Man of India'. First Indian elected to British House of Commons (Liberal, 1892). Architect of the 'Drain Theory'. Three-time president of INC (1886, 1893, 1906).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The 'CITY OF PALACES' in India is:
questions.explanation: Kolkata — once capital of British India — earned 'City of Palaces' for its colonial-era grand buildings (Victoria Memorial, Writers' Building, Raj Bhavan, Marble Palace). Udaipur is 'City of Lakes'. Mysore is 'City of Palaces' also used colloquially for the Amba Vilas + other royal palaces — but exam-standard answer is Kolkata.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The nickname 'THE MASTER BLASTER' in world cricket usually refers to:
questions.explanation: Sachin Tendulkar is widely called 'Master Blaster'. Richards was 'King Viv' / 'Sir Viv'. Sehwag is 'Nawab of Najafgarh'. Lara is 'The Prince of Trinidad'.
questions.subject: General Knowledge
